name: Individualism
summary: Individualism is the political and social philosophy that stresses the moral worth of the individual against the collectivity. In Hayek's account of its 'true' strand, society's order mostly arises from free individuals' actions rather than design, so coercive and exclusive power must be strictly limited, government confined to general rules equal for all, and central planning and egalitarian levelling rejected, while family, voluntary associations and tradition are valued. Other uses of the word, notably Tocqueville's (withdrawal into private life) and the rationalist 'false' individualism, differ.
scope: Individualism as the encyclopaedic references define it: a political and social philosophy emphasising the moral worth of the individual (Britannica, Encyclopedia.com), with its national variants. Positions are taken from Hayek's 1945 lecture 'Individualism: True and False', the one primary text those references tie to the term (Britannica reports Hayek's distinction between true and false individualism). Strands that disagree (individualist anarchism, Stirner's egoism, Durkheim's utilitarian or Kantian types, Tocqueville's critical sense) are not used for answers; liberalism and libertarianism sources are not used, being related ideologies.
